Sanford  Fagadau 


\HllO  im'O  IVH 


SIMON  FAGADAU 
AND  HIS  SON 


SANFORD  FAGADAU 


The  continuation  of  a famous  family  dinasty  from  the  Dorohoi 
Town. 

To  every  descendent  from  Dorohoi,  whatever  relates  to  the 
Fagadau  family  brings  respectfulness  and  beautifull  memories  about 
family  members  whose  activities  for  the  Jewish  community  should  be 
rememberred  and  eternally  mentioned  in  the  Pantheon  of  the  Jewish 
people. 

One  of  them  is  Simon  Fagadau  who  was  born  in  Dorohoi  in  the 
1900  and  died  in  Dallas,  Texas,  in  the  U.S.A.  in  1972. 

Simon  Fagadau,  one  of  the  few  Jewish  youngsters  that  left 
Dorohoi  then,  in  1918,  thanks  to  his  parents  insistence,  who  saw  in 
him  extraordinary  talents  and  qualities,  arrived  at  the  Sorbone 
University  in  Paris  to  learn  engineering  and  then  finished  his  studies 
as  a Petroleum  Engineering  at  the  Pitsburg  University  in  the  U.S.A. 


niir^i  nnn»  nnn 


94 


Simon  PagHdfiu  developed  an  extraordinary  and  perfect  engineering 
career  in  the  U.S.A.  and  filled  senior  jobs  in  different  firms. 

According  to  the  best  family  tradition  that  he  learned  at  his 
parents  home  in  Dorohoi,  he  was  allways  in  touch  with  the  Jewish 

community  in  the  U.S.A.  and  helped  a lot  to  advance  and  solve  social 
problems  for  the  community. 

For  a time  he  was  president  of  the  famous  Emanuel  Temple  in  the 
U.S.A.  as  his  father  was  the  main  synagougue  director  of  the  Beith 
Shlomo  Temple  in  Dorohoi. 

Simon  Fagadau  was  active  in  fund  raising  for  the  United  Jewish 
Appeal  (UJA)  and  Joint  Distribution  Committee  (JDC)  as  well  as  an 
all  Zionist  activities  for  Israel. 

Sanford  Fagadau  who  continues  his  fathers  activities,  says 
about  his  dear  father: 

"I  had  the  priviledge  of  working  with  my  father  for  some  15 
yars  he  was  my  good  friend.  He  was  extremely  intelligent  and 
had  a captivating  charm.  He  allways  had  a smile  on  his  face, 
was  never  to  busy  to  talk  to  or  help  a friend  or  a stranger  and 
was  well-liked  and  respected  by  his  peers  both  proffesionally 
and  as  a participant  in  the  Jewish  and  non  Jewish 
community." 


Sanford  Fagadau  was  born  in  the  U.S.A.  in  1928,  the  son  of 
Simon  Fagadau  absorbed  the  tradition  of  the  forefathers  and  feels 
himself  bound  to  his  family  roots,  in  all  that  maters. 

Sanford  is  pround  of  his  honorable  family,  his  wife,  Jeanne 
Marilyin  (Malkoff)  Fagadau  and  his  children,  dr.  Warren  (Chip) 
F agadau,  Leslie  Ann  Shechter  and  Thomas  H.  Fagadau. 

Gratuated  from  the  Ohio  State  University  with  the  B.Sc.  Degree, 
Geology,  1947,  the  M.Sc  Degree,  Geology,  1949  and  the  Ph.  D.  Degree, 
Geology,  1952. 

Like  his  father  and  grandfather,  Sanford  is  active  in  social  Jewish 
fields  and  amongst  others: 

1992  - Present:  BOARD  MEMBER,  United  way  of  Dallas;  Jewish 
Federation  of  Greater  Dallas:  Council  of  Jewish  Fe-deration 
(National). 

1990-93  Vice-President,  Temple  Emanuel. 

1989-91  President,  Jewish  Federation  of  Greater  Dallas. 

1988-90  President,  Community  Homes  for  Adults,  Inc.  (Jewish 
Retardet). 

1986-88  President,  The  Dallas  Home. 

Sanford  Fagadau  continues  to  take  care  of  the  honorable 
heritage  of  his  father  and  grandfather^as  well  as  of  the  pride  of  such 
personalities  from  the  Dorohoi  descendants  here  and  everywhere  in 
the  world  that  add  respect  to  their  exemplary  actions  for  the  public 
welfare.

The  Search  for  the  Regenstreichs 

My  name  is  Gene  Starn.  My  wife,  Elaine,  is  a Regenstreich.  Her  father,  Jacob,  was 
born  in  MIhaileni,  Romania,  is  1893.  His  father,  Mendel,  was  also  born  there  in  1857,  and  his 
father,  Eliezer  (Lazar,  they  called  him),  about  1832.  We  don't  know  if  he  was  bom  in  Mihaileni, 
or  he  came  there  from  someplace  else. 

I am  a writer  and  a genealogist 

In  the  search  for  my  wife's  family,  we  have  discovered  many  hundreds  of  people  with  the 
same  last  name,  or  a variation  of  it  - Regenstreif,  mostly,  or  Regen  or  Regent  or  even 
Regenstaff.  In  fact,  I have  sent  an  inquiry  world-wide  for  anyone  who  thinks  they  are  a part  of 
the  Regenstreich  family  to  contact  me  so  that  I can  add  them  to  the  family  hlsto^  I intend  to 
write  about  this  illustrious  group  of  people. 

Where  did  they  begin?  God  only  knows,  but  I think  they  may  have  come  from  the 
Austro-Hungary  empire  of  Joseph  11.  He  toterated  Jews  more  fairly  during  his  reign,  but  after  his 
death,  a wave  of  anti-semitism  swept  through  the  country,  and  the  Regenstreich's  moved 
onward.  One  branch  may  have  gone  to  Italy,  another  to  America,  but  most  went  into  nearby 
Romania,  possibly  even  founding  the  town  of  Rhegin  in  certtral  Romania.  Eventually,  many  of 
the  Regenstreichs  settled  in  Mihaileni  or  Dorohot  in  what  is  now  northern  Romania. 

in  our  search  we  have  found  more  than  100  who  are  direct  descendants  of  my  wife's 
great  grandfather,  Eliezer.  These  are  the  easiest  to  find,  because  we  knew  many  of  them  during 
our  lifetime. 

What  is  fascinating  about  our  research  is  the  other  hundreds  with  the  same  or  similar 
name  that  we  have  been  unable,  so  far,  to  tie  together. 

So  far,  we  have  found  at  least  seven  other  "branches"  that  are  awaiting  some  deciding 
clue  that  will  hook  them  into  the  main  branch  of  the  family.  These  are  the  unmatched  branches: 

1)  The  CANADA  connection.  They  call  themselves  RegenSTRElF  and 
originated  in  Dorohoi,  Romania.  Most  are  now  living  in  the  Montreal  region.  The 
founding  father  of  this  branch  is  Shmuel  Dov  Regenstreif,  born  in  1836.  His  son, 
Abraham,  fathered  Aaron,  Beryl,  Louis,  Sarah,  Etde,  Ida,  Max,  Benjamin,  Martin 
and  Arthur. 

2)  Nathan  Regenstreich,  bom  in  1840,  fathered  another  branch  with  sons 
Benjamin  and  Joseph.  Someone  told  me  the  family  had  a big  restaurant  in  Bucharest 
around  the  time  of  the  first  World  War.  I call  this  my  NEW  JERSEY  connection, 
because  tv^  of  the  brothers  live  there. 


3)  A remnant  of  the  RUMANIAN  connection  lives  in  BurcharesL  Dan 
Regenstreif,  born  in  Mihaileni,  says  his  father,  Ira,  died  in  1948.  His  grandfather  was 
named  Sruel,  who  died  in  1940.  Dan's  uncles,  Aaron  and  Avrum,  emigrated  to  Israel, 
but  died  in  1972  and  1974.  Hutsgii,  or  something  like  that,  died  in  Romania  in  1991. 
He  also  mentioned  an  aunt,  Chaya  Sura. 

4)  We  have  a CATHOLIC  connection,  too.  Joseph  Robert  Regenstreif  (1898- 
1969)  is  supposed  to  have  come  from  Austro-Hungary  to  the  U.S.  But  maybe  he 
stopped  off  in  Romania  first  His  son,  Harry,  contacted  us  from  Ann  Arbor,  Mich.
